world_money_map.summary: The picture remains mixed rather than broadly risk-on or risk-off, but the near-term U.S. funding-risk assessment has become more precise. Bank reserves were $3.0365T on Sep. 9 and ON RRP was only about $5.3B on Sep. 11. Relative to Q2 nominal GDP of $32.486T, reserves plus ON RRP are roughly 9.4% of GDP. A Federal Reserve FEDS Note published Aug. 26 finds that Treasury issuance shocks become much more powerful for repo rates when Fed-provided liquidity is below 10% of GDP. Sep. 15 is therefore a high-information stress test because major estimated-tax payments coincide with settlement of 3-year, 10-year and 30-year Treasury coupon securities and several bills. Latest validated repo data remain calm, so this is a conditional vulnerability rather than a current funding crisis. The Sep. 15-16 FOMC decision remains the dominant policy event risk.
world_money_map.liquidity: SHORT-TERM US EASING, BUT CURRENT FED LIQUIDITY ~9.4% OF GDP AND MORE SENSITIVE TO ISSUANCE SHOCKS
world_money_map.credit: NO VALIDATED BROAD STRESS SIGNAL YET

money_flows.title: Treasury cash runoff temporarily released reserves
money_flows.summary: On the Fed's Sep. 9 balance sheet, the Treasury General Account fell by about $101B from the prior Wednesday while reserve balances rose by about $107B. With the Fed securities portfolio nearly unchanged, Treasury cash movements were the dominant observable source of the reserve increase.

money_flows.title: Quarter-end Treasury cash rebuilding can reverse part of that easing
money_flows.summary: Treasury's Aug. 3 financing estimate assumes a $950B end-September cash balance. The Sep. 9 TGA stood near $844B. Because ON RRP is nearly exhausted, a future TGA rebuild has less buffer than in earlier cycles and can transmit more directly to reserves/private liquidity.
money_flows.invalidation: Treasury materially undershoots its $950B cash target, or offsetting Fed/liability flows replenish reserves.
money_flows.source: U.S. Treasury Aug. 3 borrowing estimate; Fed H.4.1; NY Fed/FRED ON RRP

money_flows.title: Sep. 15 concentrates potential repo demand and cash drainage
money_flows.direction: BANK/MMF CASH -> TREASURY / DEALER FINANCING DEMAND
money_flows.summary: Sep. 15 combines a major estimated-tax payment date with settlement of 3-year, 10-year and 30-year Treasury coupon securities and several bills. Fed research shows that issuance and dealer Treasury holdings are much more rate-sensitive when reserves plus ON RRP are below 10% of GDP; current aggregate Fed liquidity is roughly 9.4% of Q2 nominal GDP.
money_flows.invalidation: Repo rates and upper percentiles remain orderly through the cash/settlement window, standing repo usage stays negligible, and TGA/reserves show no meaningful tightening.
money_flows.source: Federal Reserve FEDS Note Aug. 26, 2026; IRS 2026 tax calendar; U.S. Treasury tentative auction schedule; Fed H.4.1; BEA/FRED GDP

money_flows.title: Funding markets have not yet confirmed reserve scarcity
money_flows.summary: Latest validated repo observations remained orderly: SOFR was 3.62% on Sep. 10, the SOFR 99th percentile was 3.70%, and the TGCR 99th percentile was 3.65%. Standing repo operations remain available to limit economically significant upward pressure.
money_flows.source: NY Fed data via FRED; New York Fed standing repo framework

money_flows.title: Global policy is not moving in one easing direction
money_flows.direction: CASH / BONDS REPRICE TOWARD HIGHER REQUIRED RETURNS
money_flows.summary: The ECB raised all three key policy rates by 25 bp on Sep. 10. In the U.S., the last FOMC target range was 3.50%-3.75% and the next decision is Sep. 16. This argues against treating the current environment as a synchronized global liquidity boom.
money_flows.source: ECB Sep. 10 decision; Federal Reserve calendar

opportunities.title: Preserve cash optionality through the Sep. 15 funding test and Sep. 16 FOMC
opportunities.thesis: The expected value of forcing a broad directional macro position is not yet demonstrated. Current Fed liquidity is in a more issuance-sensitive zone, but actual repo stress has not appeared. Sep. 15 provides a direct falsifiable test before the FOMC: if repo rates remain contained despite taxes and settlements, the scarcity thesis weakens; if broad secured-funding pressure appears, the risk case strengthens materially.
opportunities.invalidation: A clear asymmetric opportunity appears with independently verified flow support before these events resolve.
opportunities.source: Fed FEDS Note Aug. 26; IRS tax calendar; Treasury auction schedule; NY Fed repo data; FOMC calendar

risks.title: Sep. 15 can expose repo-market capacity constraints
risks.summary: Fed research finds that when reserves plus ON RRP are below 10% of GDP, Treasury coupon issuance has historically had a much larger impact on TGCR-IORB. Current Fed liquidity is roughly 9.4% of Q2 nominal GDP. Sep. 15 also combines estimated-tax cash drains with Treasury settlements. This raises sensitivity to a funding shock but does not establish that one will occur.
risks.invalidation: TGCR, SOFR and their upper percentiles remain contained; standing repo usage remains negligible; EFFR stays anchored; and post-event TGA/reserve data show adequate liquidity.

risks.title: TGA rebuild can become a near-term liquidity drain, but stress is conditional
risks.summary: A TGA rebuild toward Treasury's $950B quarter-end assumption can absorb private liquidity with little remaining ON RRP buffer. It becomes a stronger market-risk signal only if funding-market indicators confirm scarcity.
risks.invalidation: The TGA does not rebuild materially, reserve-supplying offsets dominate, or funding markets remain orderly despite the reserve decline.

risks.title: Rates can stay high even if growth remains resilient
risks.summary: August payrolls rose 162k with unemployment at 4.1%, while August CPI was 3.4% y/y and 0.4% m/m. A resilient labor market plus elevated inflation can keep required returns high.
risks.invalidation: Inflation falls faster than expected and policy guidance turns materially more accommodative without a growth shock.

causal_chains.title: Treasury cash drawdown -> reserve injection
causal_chains.summary: TGA falls -> Treasury spends cash held at the Fed -> payments land in private bank deposits -> bank reserves rise -> short-term balance-sheet liquidity improves. This mechanism does not prove a durable bull regime.

causal_chains.title: Low Fed liquidity + coupon settlement + tax payments -> repo sensitivity
causal_chains.summary: Reserves plus ON RRP fall below roughly 10% of GDP -> repo rates become more sensitive to Treasury issuance/dealer financing demand -> coupon settlements increase financing demand while tax payments drain bank/MMF cash -> TGCR/SOFR can rise -> FHLBs may reallocate from fed funds toward repo -> EFFR can face upward pressure -> forced balance-sheet adjustment becomes more plausible. Standing repo operations and reserve-management purchases can interrupt this chain.
causal_chains.source: Federal Reserve FEDS Note Aug. 26, 2026; IRS calendar; Treasury auction schedule

causal_chains.title: Quarter-end TGA rebuild -> reserve drain -> funding stress only if reserve/repo capacity binds
causal_chains.summary: Treasury cash accumulation drains private liquidity; near-zero ON RRP reduces buffering capacity; but stress requires usable reserves or repo-market lending/intermediation capacity to become scarce. Confirm with TGCR/SOFR percentiles, EFFR-IORB and standing-repo usage rather than aggregate reserves alone.
causal_chains.source: Treasury financing estimate + Fed balance-sheet mechanics + Fed/NY Fed repo research

causal_chains.title: Energy inflation -> policy restraint -> higher discount rates
causal_chains.summary: Energy pressure -> higher inflation uncertainty -> central banks maintain or raise restrictive rates -> sovereign yields / required returns rise -> long-duration valuations face compression unless earnings or growth expectations compensate.
causal_chains.source: ECB Sep. 10 decision; BLS Aug. CPI

discoveries.title: Reserve growth and Fed asset growth are not the same thing
discoveries.summary: Large reserve changes can come from liability-side shifts such as the TGA even when Fed securities holdings barely change.

discoveries.title: Near-zero ON RRP changes Treasury-liquidity transmission
discoveries.summary: With ON RRP near zero, Treasury cash rebuilding has less capacity to be absorbed by an ON RRP decline and can transmit more directly to reserves/private liquidity.
discoveries.source: NY Fed source via FRED ON RRP series

discoveries.title: Reserve drain is not the same as funding stress
discoveries.summary: A falling reserve balance is a liquidity headwind, not a mechanical sell signal. Funding-market confirmation is required.
discoveries.source: NY Fed/FRED SOFR; New York Fed standing repo framework

discoveries.title: Repo-market capacity can bind before aggregate reserve demand
discoveries.summary: Recent Fed research shows that day-to-day repo pricing is strongly driven by Treasury issuance, dealer inventory and MMF cash, and that repo-rate sensitivity rises sharply when reserves plus ON RRP fall below roughly 10% of GDP. At current levels, the system is already near 9.4%, so aggregate reserves can still look ample while repo capacity becomes the marginal constraint.
discoveries.source: Federal Reserve FEDS Note Aug. 26, 2026; Fed H.4.1; BEA/FRED GDP

changes_since_previous: Current reserves plus ON RRP are roughly 9.4% of Q2 nominal GDP, placing the system in the Fed research bucket where Treasury issuance shocks have historically had much larger repo-rate effects.
Sep. 15 is now identified as a high-information funding stress test because estimated-tax payments coincide with multiple Treasury settlements.
The reserve-scarcity model has been upgraded: repo-market capacity, dealer financing demand and MMF cash supply can become binding before aggregate bank reserve demand does.
Latest validated repo observations remain orderly, so the new finding raises conditional risk rather than establishing a current funding crisis.
The decision-support stance remains WAIT through the Sep. 15 funding test and Sep. 16 FOMC.
unknowns: The Sep. 15-16 FOMC decision and guidance are not known yet and can materially change the rates/liquidity interpretation.
The exact net cash impact of Sep. 15 Treasury settlements and estimated-tax payments is not known in advance.
Treasury's $950B end-September cash balance is an assumption, not a guaranteed realized level.
It remains unknown whether current repo-market capacity is sufficient to absorb the Sep. 15 combination of settlement demand and tax-driven cash outflows without measurable rate pressure.
The current liquidity mechanics do not yet establish a reliable directional forecast for equities, crypto, gold, credit or the dollar.
research_frontier: Highest priority: treat Sep. 15 as a falsifiable stress test. Compare TGCR-IORB, SOFR median/75th/99th percentiles, EFFR-IORB, standing-repo usage, TGA and reserve changes against the pre-event baseline.
After the Sep. 16 FOMC decision, measure the change in the expected policy path and identify which asset classes should gain or lose from the new real-rate regime.
Quantify historically how tax dates and Treasury settlements interact when reserves plus ON RRP are below 10% of GDP, controlling for Fed reserve-management purchases and dealer/MMF balance sheets.
Build a point-in-time global liquidity composite across the Fed, ECB, BoJ, PBoC, Treasury cash balances, dollar funding and major stablecoin supply.
Establish the immutable Money Intelligence forecast ledger before making the first directional forecast that clears the evidence bar.

source_notes.title: Federal Reserve FEDS Note - Aug. 26, 2026
source_notes.summary: Repo-rate sensitivity to Treasury issuance rises sharply at low Fed liquidity. $50B net coupon issuance is associated with less than 1 bp of TGCR-IORB pressure above 12% of GDP but almost 10 bp below 10% of GDP. Day-to-day repo moves are driven strongly by issuance, dealer holdings and MMF cash supply.
